9748               cv567
9749               	;
9750               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9751               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9752               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9753               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9754               	; 	' runs every pass.
9755               	; 	'
9756               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9757               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9758               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9759               	; 	'
9760               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9761               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9762               	; 	'
9763               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9764               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9765               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9766               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9767               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9768               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9769               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9770               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9771               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9772               	; 	'
9773               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9774               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9775               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9776               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9777               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9778               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9779               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9780               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9781               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9782               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9783               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the
9784               	; 	' flight looking busy.
9785               	; 	'
9786               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.
9787               	; 	'
9788               	; 	' THE KOP ARRIVING ON THIS FLOOR OUTRANKS IT. This used to override the
9789               	; 	' flee as well as the climb, so for the whole of the run he held one
9790               	; 	' heading no matter where Kelly was -- and ran straight into him without
9791               	; 	' appearing to notice he was there. The flee above has already worked out
9792               	; 	' which way is away; clearing the run simply lets it stand.

9880               	;
9881               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9882               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9883               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9884               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9885               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9886               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9887               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9888               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9889               	; 	'
9890               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9891               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9892               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9893               	; 	'
9894               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9895               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9896               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9897               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9898               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9899               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9900               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9901               	; 	'
9902               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9903               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9904               	; 	'
9905               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9906               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9907               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9908               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9909               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9910               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9911               	; 	'
9912               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9913               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9914               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9915               	; 	' before any of this.
9916               	; 	'
9917               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9918               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9919               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9920               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
9921               	; 	' journey.
9922               	; 	'
9923               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
9924               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
9925               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.

10386               	;
10387               	; 	' ======================================================================
10388               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10389               	; 	' ======================================================================
10390               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10391               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10392               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10393               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10394               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10395               	; 	'
10396               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10397               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10398               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10399               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10400               	; 	' broken.
10401               	; 	'
10402               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10403               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10404               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10405               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10406               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10407               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10408               	; 	'
10409               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10410               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10411               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10412               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10413               	; coll_obst:
10414               cvb_COLL_OBST

10735               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10736               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10737               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10738               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10739               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10740               	; 	' away from.
10741               	; 	'
10742               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10743               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10744               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10745               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10746               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10747               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10748               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10749               	; 	'
10750               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10751               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10752               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10753               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10754               	; 	'
10755               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10756               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10757               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10758               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10759               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10760               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10761               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10762               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10763               	; 	'

10927               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10928               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10929               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10930               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10931               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10932               	; 	'
10933               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10934               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10935               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.

10940               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10941               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go

11049               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
11050               	; 	'

11052               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11053               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11054               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11055               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11056               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11057               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11058               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11059               	; 	'
11060               	; 	' Deciding BEFORE drawing costs one test and cannot race the ISR at all:
11061               	; 	' the mirror never holds a position to be caught with.

11112               	; 	' KELLY'S HAT DOES NOT FLASH WHEN HE IS HIT. It used to alternate to white

11115               	; 	' That argument no longer holds: the knockback still throws him, the HUD's
11116               	; 	' digits still drop by nine, and the hit now has a sound that is allowed to
11117               	; 	' finish. Three signals for one event, and the flash was the least legible
11118               	; 	' of them -- a two-frame colour swap on a 16 px hat, during the one moment
11119               	; 	' the player is looking at where they are being pushed.
11120               	; 	'
11121               	; 	' Dropping it retires `kcol` with it: the hat is C_KHAT always, so the
11122               	; 	' colour goes straight into the SPRITE calls below and the per-pass
11123               	; 	' variable, its assignment and two nested IFs all go.

11126               	; 	' KELLY IS SPRITES 0, 1 AND 2 and nothing else ever is -- the VDP drops
11127               	; 	' the highest-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so the lowest
11128               	; 	' slots are the ones that can never disappear, and the player is the one
11129               	; 	' thing that must never disappear.

11131               	; 	' THE BAND SPRITES SHARE A y ON PURPOSE. Slots 0 and 1 both sit at ky and
11132               	; 	' between them cover rows 0-15; slot 2 sits at ky+16. Boxes 0/1 and box 2
11133               	; 	' never share a scanline, so an actor costs at most TWO boxes on any line

11135               	; 	' cost just as much as a full one. Two actors meeting is four, exactly

12167               	; 	' ======================================================================
12168               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12169               	; 	' ======================================================================
12170               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12171               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12172               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12173               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12174               	; 	'
12175               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12176               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12177               	; 	'
12178               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12179               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12180               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12181               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12182               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12183               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12184               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12185               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12186               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12187               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12188               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12189               	; esc_tick:
12190               cvb_ESC_TICK

12192               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12193               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12194               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).

12214               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12215               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12216               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12217               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12218               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12219               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12220               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12221               	; 	'
12222               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12223               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12224               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12225               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12226               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12227               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12228               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12525               	;
12526               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12527               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12528               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12529               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12530               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12531               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12532               	; 	'
12533               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12534               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12535               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12536               	; 	'
12537               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12538               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12539               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12540               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12541               	; 	'
12542               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12543               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12544               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12545               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12546               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12547               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12548               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12549               	; 	'
12550               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12551               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12552               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12553               	; 	'
12554               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12555               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12556               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

12899               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12900               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12901               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12902               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12903               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12904               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).

12907               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12908               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12909               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12910               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12911               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12912               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12913               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12914               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12915               	; 	'
12916               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12917               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12918               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12919               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12920               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12921               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12922               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12923               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12924               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12925               	; 	'
12926               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12927               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12928               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12929               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12930               	; 	'

13001               	;
13002               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.
13003               	; 	'
13004               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
13005               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13006               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13007               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
13008               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the

13810               	;
13811               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13812               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13813               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13814               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13815               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13816               	; 	'
13817               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13818               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13819               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13820               	; 	'
13821               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13822               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13823               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13824               	; 	'
13825               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13826               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13827               	; 	'
13828               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13829               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13830               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13831               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13832               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13833               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13834               	; 	'
13835               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13836               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13837               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13838               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13839               	; 	'
13840               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13841               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13842               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13843               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)

13960               	;
13961               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13962               	; 	'
13963               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13964               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13965               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13966               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13967               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13968               	; 	'
13969               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13970               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13971               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13972               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13973               	; 	' counting stops.
13974               	;
13975               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13976               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13977               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13978               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13979               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13980               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13981               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13982               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13983               	; 	'
13984               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13985               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13986               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14057               	; 	' to exactly thirteen so the box has straight edges, and column 10 puts it

14286               	;
14287               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14288               	; 	'
14289               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14290               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14291               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14292               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14293               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14294               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14295               	; 	'
14296               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14297               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14298               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14299               	; 	'
14300               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14301               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14302               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14303               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14304               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14305               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14306               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14307               	; 	'
14308               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14309               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14310               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14311               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14312               	; 	'
14313               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14314               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14315               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14316               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14317               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14318               	; 	'
14319               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14320               	; 	' did not finish.
14321               	; pause_beat:
14322               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14684               	;
14685               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14686               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14687               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14688               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14689               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14690               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14691               	;
14692               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14693               	; 	'
14694               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14695               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14696               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14697               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14698               	; 	'
14699               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14700               	; 	'
14701               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14702               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14703               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14704               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14705               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14706               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14707               	; 	'
14708               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14709               	; 	'
14710               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14711               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14712               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14713               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14714               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14715               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14716               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14717               	; 	'
14718               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14719               	; 	'
14720               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14721               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14722               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14723               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14724               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14725               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14726               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14727               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14728               	; 	'
14729               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14730               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14731               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14732               	; 	'
14733               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14734               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14735               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14736               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14737               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14738               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14739               	; 	'
14740               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
14741               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
14742               	; 	'
14743               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14744               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14745               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14746               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14747               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14748               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14749               	; 	'
14750               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14751               	; 	'
14752               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14753               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the

14957               	;
14958               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14959               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14960               	; 	'
14961               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14962               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14963               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14964               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14965               	; 	'
14966               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14967               	; 	'
14968               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14969               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14970               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14971               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14972               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14973               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14974               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14975               	; 	'
14976               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14977               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14978               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14979               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14980               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14981               	; 	'
14982               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14983               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14984               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14985               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14986               	; 	#if TI994A
14987               	; 	BANK 2
14988      0128     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15126               	;
15127               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
15128               	; 	'
15129               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
15130               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
15131               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
15132               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
15133               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
15134               	; 	'
15135               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
15136               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
15137               	;

15652               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15653               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15654               	; 	'
15655               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15656               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15657               	; 	' being small sprites.
15658               	; 	'
15659               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15660               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15661               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15662               	; 	'
15663               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15664               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15665               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15666               	;
15667               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15668               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16924               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16925               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16926               	; 	'
16927               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16928               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16929               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16930               	; 	'
16931               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16932               	; 	' blit is
16933               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16934               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16935               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16936               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16937               	; 	'
16938               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16939               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16940               	; 	'
16941               	; 	' template ids:
16942               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16943               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16944               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16945               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16946               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16947               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16948               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16949               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16950               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16951               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16952               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16953               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16954               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16955               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16956               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
16957               	;
16958               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
